A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with matching authors, framework and core experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original intervention, early-stopping, influence-structure and mode-readout results on GSM8K, CommonsenseQA and StrategyQA, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds intervention/readout robustness tests, additional model comparisons and GSM8K mode analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds a direct LM-head readout to the diagnostic framework, bypassing gold-answer conditioning during influence estimation. The core intervention procedure and existing latent models are retained. The learned RQ3 probe is not new: it was already documented in v2 Appendix D.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K/GSM8K-Aug, CommonsenseQA and StrategyQA for the same underlying reasoning tasks. The new GSM8K mode analysis examines retained data; additional paradigms and backbones expand model configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D newly evaluates Sim-CoT variants in GSM8K RQ1/RQ2 comparisons (Figures 19–20); v2 only cited Sim-CoT. The existing main Coconut, CODI and CoT-SFT comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New experiments extend RQ2 to mean/Gaussian interventions and direct LM-head KL readouts. They also evaluate Sim-CoT and additional Coconut backbones: Qwen3-1.7B, Mistral-7B, DeepSeek-R1-Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama3-8B. Appendix F.3 introduces filtered numeric-answer mode analysis on GSM8K. Existing splits and training schedules are retained.

E4.justification: v2 already compared six intervention operators for RQ1. v3 substantially extends robustness analysis to RQ2 operator and readout dependence (C.4–C.5), tests generality across additional paradigms/backbones (D–E), and adds supporting GSM8K mode analysis (F.3).

E5.justification: The generic error-bar description and deterministic/fixed-seed language remain. New bar plots follow the existing uncertainty presentation, without new disclosed run counts, confidence levels, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures. RQ3 rollout counts remain symbolic.

E6.justification: Figures 17–23 add substantial results, including non-local influence under alternative protocols, relatively more local Sim-CoT connectivity, additional backbone profiles and GSM8K mode trajectories. Figure 7 also revises CoT-Qwen3-4B structural-summary values; late-in decreases from approximately 0.07 to 0.04. Most earlier plots and the corresponding dense heatmaps remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 19 newly defines influence through KL divergence between baseline and intervened LM-head distributions. Existing SCM, intervention, early-stopping, structural-summary and probe mathematics remain equivalent. The newly numbered definitions restate existing content; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: step-resolved causal evaluation, heterogeneous step importance, non-local influence and a gap between output preference and representational commitment. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v3 more explicitly qualifies influence graphs as protocol-conditioned, links Sim-CoT locality to step-aligned supervision, and adds scaling/filtering caveats and concrete supervision/stopping implications. Central interpretations remain stable. However, v2's explicit warning that zeroing may induce off-manifold distribution shifts is removed.

D1.justification: Training recipes, learning rates, answer templates, probe-fitting details, dataset counts and the code link are retained across the matched appendices. Beyond the new analysis definitions and model configurations, v3 supplies no substantive additional implementation or access information; detailed recipes and sample counts for the new experiments remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands its causal-mediation and mechanistic-intervention grounding, adding works such as Robins and Greenland, Imai, Vig, Meng, Conmy and Mueller. A new paragraph covers reinforcement learning and large reasoning models. Turner et al. is removed; publication updates to retained works are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 7 to Section 2, the RQ sections gain separate Implications subsections, and Discussion is extensively rewritten while incorporating v2 Appendix E. Limitations moves into the main text, appendices are reorganized, and the probe description is reconciled with existing appendix details.

P2.justification: v3 switches the main text to two columns, redraws Figure 2, rearranges Figure 7 into a two-by-two display, and adds Figures 17–23. New Table 1 redisplays the existing intervention operators; the dataset table is renumbered. Many earlier graphs and heatmaps are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new operator/readout robustness tests address important weaknesses in the earlier evidence, while additional models test generalizability and the revised probe description resolves an internal inconsistency. These provide a limited net quality gain, tempered by sparse reproducibility details for the new experiments and removal of the explicit off-manifold limitation.
